title: Packaging & Showcasing Your Game 📦
description: Optimise, package, test, and prepare your capstone for portfolio presentation.

slides.title: Optimisation Pass ⚡
slides.content:
# Polish Performance

Before building, ensure your game runs smoothly:

* Use **stat fps**, **stat unit** to check frame rate. Target 60 FPS.
* Switch to **Shader Complexity** view (Alt+8) and simplify any red materials.
* Reduce light overlaps (use baked lighting for static objects).
* Disable **Tick** on actors that don't need it (the room props).
* Check **Texture sizes**: no 4K textures for small objects.
* Use **LODs** on distant meshes if any (not critical for a small room).

Run a full playthrough and note any stutter.

quizData.question: Which console command shows detailed frame timing breakdown?
quizData.explanation: stat unit shows Frame, Game, Draw, and GPU times in milliseconds.

slides.title: Packaging for Windows 🖥️
slides.content:
# Build Your .exe

1. Set **Project Settings → Maps & Modes** → Game Default Map to `EscapeRoom`.
2. In **Packaging** settings, ensure **Build Configuration** is **Shipping**.
3. Add your main menu level (if created) as the first map in the package list.
4. Go to **File → Package Project → Windows** (or Mac).
5. Choose an output folder and wait for cooking.
6. Test the packaged build thoroughly – interaction, UI, audio, and win condition.
7. Zip the folder and you have a standalone game!

slides.title: Creating a Main Menu (Optional) 🏠
slides.content:
## Professional Touch

Create a second level `MainMenu` with a Widget Blueprint showing:
* Title "Escape the Room"
* Start button (Open Level to `EscapeRoom`)
* Quit button
* Credits (your name!)

Set this as the Game Default Map. Add a simple background image and some ambient music.

This makes your capstone feel complete and portfolio‑ready.

quizData.question: You should test the packaged build separately from Play in Editor.
quizData.explanation: Packaged builds can behave differently (cooking issues, missing assets). Always test the final build.

slides.title: Showcasing Your Work 📸
slides.content:
# Portfolio Ready

* Record a **gameplay video** (OBS, ShareX) and upload to YouTube/Vimeo.
* Take high‑res **screenshots** (F9).
* Write a short **design document** explaining the puzzle and technical highlights.
* Share the packaged game on [itch.io](https://itch.io) or as a downloadable link.

Congratulations! You've built a complete Unreal Engine game from scratch. 🎉

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Keep Learning

Use this capstone as a springboard. Add more puzzles, multiplayer, or VR support. The Unreal Engine community and documentation are your next best friends.
